description.to:
Outcome: Today both tools cover five models only (Section, Item, PublishedItem, MediaAsset, PublishedMediaAsset; docs/multi-tenancy.md and docs/migrations/copy-backend.md), and they disagree on media keys: copy-backend and import-markus write media/<tenant>/..., while the one-key rule says media/<srcPath>. Extend both to every tenant-owned model and table from PPY-cd5926: stamp tenantId, rewrite every global key value with the tenant prefix, give corpora tenant-unique ids (rewriting corpusId and corpus-prefixed keys on References), move S3 objects to tenants/<tenant>/... with row paths to match, copy the Cyclotron store prefix (<s3Prefix>-<tenant>), and report rows without a tenant as a count that must reach zero. Dry run by default, idempotent, refuses rows of another tenant, prints a plan per model. This is what moves Threat Intelligence into the shared stack and what every dedicated site runs to adopt its fixed tenant.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): src/papyrus_content (adopt-tenant-data command, copy_backend module and its CLI), docs/multi-tenancy.md, docs/migrations/copy-backend.md, features/tenant-scoping.feature (existing, PPY-109133).

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-adoption-complete.feature):
Scenario: A single-tenant backend is copied into a tenant completely
    Given a backend with References, Messages, Assignments, corpora, media and reader votes and no tenant
    When copy-backend --stamp-tenant "threat-intelligence" --apply runs twice
    Then the second run creates, updates and copies nothing
    And the target reports zero rows without a tenant

Scenario: Adoption never touches another tenant
    Given a target where "beta" already owns a row with the same id
    When "alpha" is adopted
    Then the row is listed as a conflict and the apply writes nothing

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-ce6207, PPY-752480, PPY-f60a1e, PPY-ef2c57. Blocks PPY-bdc4ee, PPY-b99fc0, PPY-e882ee, PPY-e1d26f, PPY-13fbea, PPY-7438d9. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-109133, PPY-e277e3.

Testing: pytest with recorded fixtures; a sandbox copy of a real backend (Pilobolus, pre-production) as the rehearsal; manifests compared.
Rollout: Command only; each run is an operator action with a dry run first and Ryan's approval for production backends.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: a corpus id rewrite breaks references from outside the table (Cyclotron stores, monitor configs, S3 vector metadata). Mitigation: the dry run lists every outside reference it knows, and the Cyclotron and monitor configs are rewritten in the same run.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
